get.description:

post.description:
Import a draft (markdown + YAML front matter). Creates the document on first import.

``base_version``: the version the draft was written on (0: the draft creates the
document). When a newer version changed sections (or the front matter) the draft
does not have as the latest has them, the import is a 409 naming both versions and
those sections (never a silent overwrite). Without it the import works as before,
and the version carries a ``base_version_missing`` note.

200.description: Same content as an existing version

409.description: The draft's base version is older than the latest, and the draft would overwrite sections changed since

get.description: Top-level comments with their replies nested.

put.description:
A verdict on a section, bound to its revision. Send ``revision`` (the section's
content hash you read) and a verdict on text that changed since is a 409.

get.description:
Review status of every section of a version: its revision, status (approved on
this revision, stale, changes requested...), the approval it holds, owner,
reviewers, due date, open feedback by severity, and whether a publish needs it.

put.description:
Set a section's owner, reviewer assignees and due date. Send the ``lock_version``
from the section states (null for a section with none); a stale one is a 409.

get.description: Sections the caller owns or was asked to review, soonest due first.
The document's review policy, else the company's ``review_policy`` setting.

put.description:
Designated decider, mandatory reviewers, extra required sections, which sections
need approval before a publish, and whether a change requests re-review.

Save one section as the next version. Send the version and section revision you
loaded: another section changed since is fine (the edit applies on the latest
version); the same section changed since is a 409 with its current text. Approvers
edit any section; a section's owner edits their own, and their ``resolutions`` close
only that section's feedback (403 otherwise). An edit that reaches outside its
section (adds, rewrites or swallows another section) is a 422.

get.description:
Proposed replacements of section text (an agent rewrite of an approved
section), newest first.
A patch with its word diff against the section's current text.

post.description:
Accept a patch (optionally edited): the section's next revision, as a new
version. ``base_revision`` is the current revision you compared against.

Ask the organization for feedback on a version: everyone with an audience role
is notified. Comments are gathered; approval stays with the decider.

put.description: Turn each built-in job kind on or off for this document.

get.description:
The users of this company's Oracle, their roles, and whether each is active or
disabled (a removed member: kept so history keeps their name).

delete.description:
Remove a member: the same as ``POST /v1/members/{user_id}/disable`` (a member is
never deleted; their row keeps the history's names).

post.description:
Remove a member by disabling them: sign-in is refused on every path; their
connections are disconnected (revoked at the provider) and their sources recorded
as revoked, so documents citing them cannot publish; their API tokens and OAuth
grants are revoked, their runs cancelled, the open invite for their email revoked;
their approvals lapse for good; every session they signed is ended. The calls at
the providers and the runtime are made after the disable commits, outside the
review gate, and retried by the tick when they fail. The member stays in the list
(history keeps the name); an owner can restore them, and they sign in fresh. A
no-op for a disabled member.

Let a disabled member sign in again, with their role. Their approvals stay
lapsed, their tokens revoked and their connections gone: nothing else comes back.

get.description: Every API token of this company (never the secret), revoked ones included.

delete.description:
Revoke an API token. The approvals given through it lapse for good (section
verdicts and version approvals); its user's own approvals stand. Revoking twice is
a no-op.

get.description:
The approvals given through an API token, oldest first, lapsed ones included
(``lapsed_at``): what revoking it voids, or voided.
Invites, newest first: open ones unless ``status`` asks for others (or ``all``).

post.description: Pre-assign a role to an email: its first Google sign-in lands with that role.

409.description: Already a member, or an open invite exists

delete.description: Revoke an open invite. Revoking twice is a no-op; an accepted invite is a 409.

post.description:
Make a provider revoke (or runtime cancel) a disable still owes now, whatever its
backoff or its 24 hours of retries. A success drops Oracle's copy of the credential.

Stop trying a provider revoke (or runtime cancel) a disable owes: Oracle's copy of
the credential is dropped, and the dismissal audited.

409.description: OAuth is not configured for this provider

get.description: Where the provider sends the browser back; ends on the Connections page.

delete.description:
Disconnect: revoke the grant at the provider where it has an endpoint (GitHub,
Slack, Google; best effort), record a ``source_permission`` revocation for each
source it synced, then delete Oracle's copy of the credential.

post.description:
New token: replace it (same account only). No token: refresh or re-check; when
the provider needs a fresh sign-in, returns ``authorize_url`` instead.

get.description: Every account in the company's pool, with the sweep's liveness and the fallback.

post.description:
Add an account from Claude Code's saved login, pasted verbatim.

It must be a PAIR: a credential with no refresh token cannot be kept alive, so it is
refused here rather than dying silently at its first expiry.

Start a browser sign-in: the URL to open, and the ``state`` that keys it.

The PKCE verifier stays here, keyed by ``state``; the browser never holds it.

Redeem the pasted code and add the account.

Only whoever started the sign-in may finish it, checked BEFORE the code is redeemed:
a mismatch redeems nothing and leaves the pending sign-in for its owner. Where the
account lands (its label) comes from the pending sign-in, never from this request.

put.description: Set the credential used while no account is registered (setup-token or API key).

post.description: Run the sweep now: reclaim holds, refresh credentials, read usage.

put.description:
AVAILABLE, PAUSED, DRAINING or REAUTH_REQUIRED. DRAINING marks every live hold to
move at its next turn boundary, in the same transaction.

post.description:
Exchange this account's credential now, through the same single writer as the
sweep, and say what happened.

delete.description: Remove the account; its open hold records close as ``account_removed``.

get.description: The LIVE holds: an expired one is a killed job, not a holder.

Recorded spans taken in [from, to), newest first (default: the last 7 days).

A cursor is ``<instant>|<n>``: the last ``assigned_at`` served and how many rows at
that instant were served, so ties are not dropped. Windows over 90 days, and
cursors this route did not mint, are refused.

What the user can add: each kind, whether its connector is available, and the
user's own connections it can sync with.

post.description:
Run the connector now. A rejected credential puts the source in status error;
a rate limit stops cleanly and the next sync resumes from the saved cursor.

422.description: No connector registered for the kind

post.description:

get.description: The user's items as they were at the snapshot (each at its pinned version).

Search the user's own items. Ranked by relevance x confidence weight; ``as_of``

Every entity and edge (no evidence bodies): what the Baseline screen draws.

202.description: The item is locked: the change became a proposal
The item is locked: the change became a proposal
